sources.title: The Enterprise AI Agent Readiness Checklist 2026: Security, Governance, and Scale
keyFindings: 40% of enterprise apps will integrate task-specific AI agents by end of 2026
Only 24% of orgs have full visibility into what their AI agents are doing
Agents create new attack surfaces via tool use and function calling
Multi-agent orchestration is becoming standard — specialized agents easier to monitor and govern than one monolithic agent

sources.title: A Practical Checklist for Evaluating and Governing AI Agents
keyFindings: 78% have AI agent pilots running, but only 14% have scaled to production
88% failure-before-production rate across enterprise deployments
Top barrier: output quality (32% of respondents per LangChain survey)
Only 52% run any offline evaluations before shipping
Six pre-production areas: task success, tool reliability, traceability, permission boundaries, fallback logic, accountability

sources.title: AI Agent Verification Checklist: 25 Checks Before You Deploy
keyFindings: 25 verification checks across 5 categories: functional correctness, safety/constraints, cost/resource controls, observability, production readiness
Non-negotiables: loop detection, output validation, token budget limits
Load test at 2x expected peak concurrent requests
Rollback plan under 5 minutes required
Re-run checks on prompt change, model update, tool change, or monthly

sources.title: 8 Production Readiness Checklists for Every AI Agent
keyFindings: 8 domains: architectural robustness, data pipelines, drift monitoring, observability, capacity planning, incident response, compliance, cost governance
Schema validation and drift monitoring are foundational
Centralized telemetry with consistent tagging (conversation_id, agent_version)
Role-specific dashboards: real-time alerts for engineers, cost trends for execs

sources.title: How to Ship a Production-Ready AI Agent: 9-Point Checklist for Platform Teams
keyFindings: Abstract model calls behind an interface layer for provider swap
Three guardrail layers: input (prompt injection, PII), output (validation, schema), action (confirmation before irreversible writes)
Minimum 20-30 representative eval test cases, run pre-deploy and post-model-change
Per-request, per-user, and global token budget limits enforced in code
Decision trajectory logging, not just output logging
Staged autonomy: 100% human review at launch, category-by-category removal over 2-4 weeks

sources.title: Framework for Testing AI Agents: The 30-Point Agentic Reliability Enforcement Checklist
keyFindings: 30 checks across 4 domains: cognitive health/resource governance, tool safety/execution, data integrity, human interaction/resilience
New in v1.3: Zombie Agent defense and Policy Insubordination testing
Loop detection: throw error after 3 identical tool calls with same parameters
Agents scoring below 80% classified as Experimental — unsuitable for production
EU AI Act, ISO 42001, ISO 8200, NIST AI RMF aligned

sources.title: CIO's Enterprise AI Checklist for 2026
keyFindings: 90-day rollout plan: Month 1 foundations, Month 2 data access and change management, Month 3 observability and operations
Identity: SSO, MFA, RBAC from day one
Workspace boundaries by team/function
Version history and rollback for workflows touching sensitive data
Define incident paths: how to pause agent, roll back change, revoke access

sources.title: Production Readiness Checklists for AI Agents: A Field-Tested Framework
keyFindings: Stochastic containment is non-negotiable: temperature controls, output validators, circuit breakers
Token economics: capacity planning must account for context window inflation and retry storms
Human-in-the-loop escalation pathways that function when agent itself is the failure mode
Observability requires semantic tracing: chain-of-thought extraction and embedding trajectory monitoring
Rollback velocity > perfection: canary deployments with sub-60-second kill switches
Load testing must include adversarial prompts, not just volume

sources.title: Agentic AI Implementation Checklist: 12 Steps from Pilot to Production
keyFindings: Most enterprise AI pilots are technically successful but stall before production
Top barriers: poor data readiness and unclear governance
Data quality/readiness (43%) and lack of technical maturity (43%) are top obstacles
Implementation spans 3-9 months for enterprise

sources.title: Production-Ready AI Platform: The Production Readiness Rubric
keyFindings: Self-assessed 'production-ready' teams rarely score above 35/50 on first pass
7 categories, 50 criteria rubric
Architecture: abstracted model calls, tool permission scoping, rollback paths before deployment

competitiveLandscape.summary: At least 15+ distinct checklists/articles published in 2025-2026 covering AI agent production readiness. Most converge on common themes but vary in depth and audience. Market is saturated with checklist content; differentiation requires either extreme comprehensiveness (30+ checks) or specific vertical/role targeting.
contentGaps: No single checklist integrates all angles (security, governance, evals, cost, observability, compliance) into one unified framework
Few address multi-agent system-specific failure modes beyond single-agent concerns
No checklists provide concrete pass/fail criteria with scoring thresholds linked to deployment gating
Agent-specific incident response runbooks largely absent
Little coverage of agent-specific data privacy (training data leakage through tool calls)
Token budget governance for multi-step agent chains is underexplored

commonThemes: Governance and security are the #1 blockers to production deployment
Tool permission scoping and least-privilege access are mandatory
Human-in-the-loop for irreversible actions is table stakes
Observability must include trajectory/decision logging, not just output logging
Eval-driven development with CI/CD quality gates is emerging as standard practice
Cost controls (per-request, per-user, global token budgets) are essential
Rollback plans under 5 minutes are expected
Loop/circuit-breaker detection prevents infinite cost spirals
Data readiness and infrastructure quality determine production success more than model capability
synthesis.recommendedApproach: Create a unified, actionable checklist that bridges the gap between strategic governance (for CIOs) and technical verification (for platform engineers). Organize into tiers: mandatory (blocking), recommended (risk-reducing), and aspirational (maturity-building). Include quantitative scoring thresholds for deployment decisions.
